questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.**

Many a man have (1)/ come to India from Canada (2)/ to live here permanently. (3)/ No error (4).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1, i.e., **‘Many a man have’.**

Part 1 has an error as it doesn’t observe the agreement of the verb with the subject.

**‘Many a’ **is always followed by a singular verb.

Part 1 uses ‘have’, or the plural verb, instead of the singular verb ‘has’ after ‘many a man’.

Therefore, the correct sentence will be:

**Many a man has come to India from Canada to live here permanently.**

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.**

Our cricket team (1)/ comprises of (2)/ eleven skilled players. (3)/ No error (4).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2, i.e., **‘comprises of’**.

Part 2 has an error as the correct expression is **‘comprises’ **and not **‘comprises of’**. The verb ‘comprise’, whenever used in the Active Voice (like here), is never followed by the preposition ‘of’.

Therefore, the correct sentence will be:

**Our cricket team comprises eleven skilled players.**

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.**

Our social science teacher told to (1)/ study the map of the world (2)/ for a test. (3)/ No error (4).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1, i.e., **‘Our social science teacher told to’.**

Part 1 has an error as the verb ‘tell/told’ must always be immediately followed by a noun or a pronoun.

Here, the verb ‘told’ is followed by the to-infinitive (‘to study’) and not any noun or pronoun.

Therefore, the correct sentence will be:

**Our social science teacher told us to study the map of the world.**

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select ‘No Error’.**

My sister-in-law (1)/ who lives in Chennai (2)/ have come to stay with us. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3, i.e., **‘have come to stay with us’**.

Part 3 has an error as it doesn’t follow the agreement of the verb with the subject.

A singular noun requires a singular verb.

Here, the subject (my sister-in-law) is singular but the verb (have) is plural (instead of the singular verb ‘has’), which is incorrect as the verb must agree with its subject in number.

Therefore, the correct sentence will be:

**My sister-in-law who lives in Chennai has come to stay with us**.

My friend Sahib (1)/ is one of the best football player (2)/ in the country. (3)/ No error (4).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2, i.e., **‘is one of the best football players’**.

The quantifier ‘one of’ always requires a plural noun.

Part 2 has an error as the quantifier ‘one of’ is followed by the singular noun ‘player’ (and not the plural noun ‘players’).

Therefore, the correct answer is:

**My friend Sahib is one of the best football players in the country**.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence. **

For the **(first time from)** 2009, fans in Pakistan may have a reason to celebrate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2, i.e., **‘first time since’**.

The given sentence needs improvement as the bracketed part uses the wrong preposition.

Whenever we describe the time that has elapsed from a specified point of time (2009, here), the correct preposition used before that point of time is ‘since’.

Therefore, ‘first time from’ will be replaced by ‘first time since’.

The correct sentence will be:

**For the first time since 2009, fans in Pakistan may have a reason to celebrate.**

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

Gayle’s call-up follows a relaxation in Cricket West Indies’ criteria** (in orderly to be)** eligible for selection.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1, i.e., **‘in order to be’**.

The bracketed part requires improvement as ‘in orderly to be’ is an invalid and meaningless expression.

‘In order to be’ means ‘so that’, which fits the context of the sentence.

Therefore, ‘in orderly to be’ will be replaced by ‘in order to be’.

The correct sentence will be:

**Gayle’s call-up follows a relaxation in Cricket West Indies’ criteria in order to be eligible for selection.**

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

The patriots had a comparatively modest start,** (scoring as much)** 38 in the power play.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1, i.e., **‘scoring only’**.

The bracketed part requires improvement as it uses ‘scoring as much 38’, which is grammatically incorrect. The correct expression is ‘scoring as much as 38’.

Out of the given options, it is ‘scoring only’ which, on replacing the bracketed part in the sentence, doesn’t make it grammatically incorrect.

The sentence becomes:

**The patriots had a comparatively modest start, scoring only 38 in the power play.**

All other options- ‘scoring enough’ and ‘but scores’- make the sentence either grammatically incorrect or meaningless.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

**(No sooner after)** she was jailed for her conviction on corruption charges, they began taking keen interest in her.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2, i.e., **‘soon after’**.

The bracketed part requires improvement as it uses ‘no sooner after’- an invalid expression. The grammatically correct expression is ‘no sooner than’.

Out of the given options, ‘soon after’ is grammatically correct and means the same as ‘no sooner than’.

The sentence becomes:

**Soon after she was jailed for her conviction on corruption charges, they began taking keen interest in her. **

Options 1 and 3- ‘no soon after’ and ‘sooner after’- are both incorrect as these are invalid expressions.

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

He **(is a killing)** combination of looks and talent.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1, i.e., **‘is a killer’.**

The bracketed part requires improvement as ‘a killing combination’ literally means ‘a fatal combination’, which is meaningless when used for a real person.

On the other hand, ‘a killer combination’ means ‘an amazing combination of two things put together’, which makes perfect sense here as the sentence intends to say that his looks and talent together make an amazing combination.

Therefore, ‘a killing combination’ should be replaced by ‘a killer combination’.

The sentence becomes:

**He is a killer combination of looks and talent.**

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

The project is running behind schedule** (for around)** three years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3, i.e., **‘by around’**.

The bracketed part requires improvement as it uses the wrong preposition (‘for’).

The sentence intends to tell us the number of years by which the project is late from the time it should have rightfully started at.

The correct preposition to be used in this context is ‘by’.

Therefore, the correct sentence is:

**The project is running behind by around three years.**

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

The mosquito which spreads chikungunya and dengue **(breeds on)** fresh water.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2, i.e., **‘breeds in’.**

The bracketed part requires improvement because it uses the wrong preposition (‘on’).

The sentence intends to say that the said mosquito mates and then lays its eggs in freshwater. The correct preposition in this case will be ‘in’.

Thus, the correct sentence is:

**The mosquito which spreads chikungunya and dengue breeds in fresh water.**

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

These incidents tend to pick-up post monsoon, **(there could be)** urgent need to focus on preventive measures.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1, i.e., **‘there is an’**.

The bracketed part requires improvement because it doesn’t use the article ‘an’ before ‘urgent need’.

While Options 1, 2, and 3 all use the article ‘an’, only Option 1 uses the right tense.

The first half of the sentence is in present tense (‘tend to pick-up’) and the second half, which follows as a result of the first, cannot be in the Past tense.

Options 2 and 3 use the Past tense (‘was’ and ‘could have been’) which is incorrect.

Thus, the correct sentence is:

**These incidents tend to pick-up post monsoon, there is an urgent need to focus on preventive measures.**

questions.question:
**Improve the bracketed part of the sentence.**

A surprisingly high number of cases of the flu are** (being seen) **this year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2, i.e., **‘being witnessed’**.

The verb ‘witness’ is often used in formal or technical contexts and ‘to witness something’ is ‘to observe and have knowledge of a serious or unpleasant experience or event’.

'Cases of flu’ conveys that the context is serious as it deals with a disease.

In such a context, ‘witness’ is a better verb to use.

Thus, the sentence can be improved and written as:

**A surprisingly high number of cases of the flu are being witnessed this year.**

Did you find anybody ______ there?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2, i.e., **‘else’**.

The adverb ‘else’ means ‘in addition, besides, other than you’, and it makes perfect sense in the given sentence as the sentence then means ‘Did you find anybody other than you there?’, which is coherent.

Option 1 or ‘beside’ is incorrect as it is a preposition that means ‘next to, along with’ and is always followed by a noun/pronoun which isn’t the case here.

Options 3 and 4 are incorrect as they make the sentence meaningless and grammatically incorrect.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

You think really hard, _______ ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4, i.e., **‘don’t you’.**

Clearly, the blank has to be filled with the appropriate question-tag for the given sentence.

Whenever a sentence begins with the second person pronoun (‘you’) and is followed by the infinitive of a verb (‘think’ in this case), the question-tag is formed by adding ‘don’t you?’ at the end of the sentence.

Thus, the complete sentence will be:

**You think really hard, don’t you?**

So, the correct answer is Option 4.

All other options are incorrect.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

Only ‘what’ completes the sentence without requiring any additional words.

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four given alternatives, select the one which is opposite in meaning of the given word.**

Derive
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4, i.e., **‘create’.**

To **‘derive’** is to **obtain, acquire, or extract** something. It carries the connotations of taking away something which already exists.

To **‘collect’ **is to **‘gather’ **a number of things. It also carries the connotations of taking away something which already exists.

To **‘develop’ **is to **‘grow and become more advanced’.**

To **‘infer’ **is to **‘conclude or deduce’.**

To **‘create’ **is to **bring something into existence. **It carries the connotations of bringing something new into existence.

Thus, **‘create’ **is the opposite of **‘derive’ **in meaning as the other options- ‘collect’, ‘develop’, or ‘infer’ have similar or completely unrelated meanings

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

India surprised

P: the world’s fastest

Q: growing major economy

R: the world by becoming
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1, i.e., **RPQ.**

The part of the sentence given to us is **‘India surprised’.**

The next set of words must tell us who it was that India surprised, and by doing what.

Therefore, the next in order is R or ‘the world by becoming’, as R answers both those questions.

R ends with ‘by becoming’. The next set of words must tell us what it is that India became.

This is done by P, or ‘the world’s fastest’.

Q, or ‘growing major economy’, is therefore the last in order as it supplies a subject to the adjective ‘fastest’ with which P ends.

The correct answer is RPQ and the resultant sentence is:

**India surprised the world by becoming the world’s fastest growing major economy.**

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

We can save paper

P: in electronic format

Q: and by not printing emails

R: by keeping documents
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4, i.e., **RPQ.**

The part of the sentence given to us is **‘We can save paper’**,

The next set of words must tell us how we can save paper.

This is done by R, or ‘by keeping documents’, and it is next in order.

The next set of words should tell us how we should keep documents so that we can save paper.

This is told to us by P, or ‘in electronic format’.

Therefore, the last in the sequence will be Q, or ‘and by not printing emails’, which provides additional information.

Thus, the sequence is RPQ and the resultant sentence is:

**We can save paper by keeping documents in electronic format and by not printing emails.**

questions.question:
**Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.**

Some people

P: the presence of peers

Q: feel intimidated by

R: during the learning process
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2, i.e., **QPR.**

The part of the sentence given to us is **‘Some people’.**

The next set of words should tell us something about these ‘some people’.

This is done by Q, or ‘feel intimidated by’.

The next few words should tell us what it is that those ‘some people feel intimidated by’.

This is told to us by P, or ‘the presence of peers’.

The last in the sequence is R, or ‘during the learning process’, which provides additional information about P.

Thus, the correct sequence is QPR and the resultant sentence is **‘Some people feel intimidated by the presence of peers during the learning process’**, which is grammatically correct as well as coherent.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

The part of the sentence given to us is **‘The object’.**

Once we go through all the options given to us, we realize that the first in order must be R, or ‘of adaptive e-learning’, as it helps complete the subject of the sentence.

The next set of words must tell us what ‘the object of adaptive e-learning’ is.

This is done by P, or ‘is undoubtedly’.

Thus, the last in order is Q, or ‘something fairly new’ and it completes the sentence.

Therefore, the correct order is RPQ and the resultant sentence is **‘The object of adaptive e-learning is undoubtedly something fairly new’**, which is both coherent and grammatically correct.

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Was the story written by you?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3, i.e., **‘Did you write the story?’.**

The given sentence is in Passive voice, as the form of the verb (‘was...written’) shows that something was done by the subject (‘you’) and it was ‘passive’.

Therefore, it has to be changed to Active voice, where the subject did something, and it was ‘active’.

In order to do that,

a. The object of the transitive verb in the Passive voice should become the subject of the verb in the Passive voice (‘you’ becomes the subject in place of ‘the story’).

b. The verb should be changed from the Passive voice to the Active voice without changing its tense (‘was...written’ to ‘did...write’).

Thus, the same sentence in the Active voice is **‘Did you write the story?’.**

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Options 1,2, and 4 are incorrect because they violate rule b).

questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Active/Passive Voice. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Passive/Active Voice.**

Someone stole my clutch with all its contents.

options.text: My clutch was stolen by someone with all its contents.
My clutch with all its contents was stolen.
My clutch stolen by someone with all its contents.
My clutch with all its contents were stolen.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2, i.e., **‘My clutch with all its contents was stolen’.**

The given sentence is in the Active voice, as the form of the verb (‘stole’) shows that its subject (‘Someone’) did something and was ‘active’.

Therefore, it has to be changed to the Passive voice, where something was done by the subject, and it was ‘passive’.

Therefore, ‘violates’ is the right verb in the sentence as it fits the context and completes the sense of ragging as an act that destroys the dignity of a person.

All other options do not fit the context.

questions.question: Many ______ of physical
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2, i.e., **‘complaints’.**

The sentence given to us is **‘There have been many ______ of physical and psychological injury due to ragging in colleges’.**

The sentence talks about how widespread ragging is and ‘complaints’ suits the context.

Option 1 or ‘punishments’ is incorrect as it must be followed by the preposition ‘for’ and not ‘of’.

Options 3 and 4 (‘rewards’ and ‘compliments’) don’t suit the context.

questions.question: Nowadays, it has been turned to a ______ to students
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3, i.e., **‘nightmare’.**

The sentence given to us is **‘Nowadays, it has been turned to a ______ to students and their guardians’.**

‘Nightmare’ which means ‘something so unpleasant that you want to avoid it at all costs’ suits the context of how distressing the experience of ragging can be for students.

Options 1 and 2 are incorrect as ‘disaster’ and ‘hell’ must be followed by ‘for’ and not ‘to’.

Option 4 is incorrect as ‘opportunity’ simply doesn’t suit the context.

questions.question: The ______ of ragging offer an argument.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4, i.e., **‘supporters’.**

The sentence given to us is **‘The ______ of ragging offer an argument for it’.**

Anyone who offers an argument ‘for’ ragging can only be its supporter (and not an agitator, a critic or an opponent).

Thus, the correct answer is ‘supporters’.

questions.question: As an ______ to make
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3, i.e., **‘aid’.**

The sentence given to us is **‘The supporters of ragging offer an argument for it as an ______ to make the students fit for the future’.**

Both the context (supporters of ragging offering an argument for it) as well as the article ‘an’ tell us that the correct answer is ‘aid’.

All other options are incorrect.

questions.question: The future ______ for existence.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2, i.e., **‘struggle’.**

The sentence given to us is **‘The supporters of ragging offer an argument for it as an aid to make the students fit for the future ______ for existence’.**

Considering the context (supporters of ragging giving an argument in favour of it), the correct answer is ‘struggle’: according to the supporters of ragging, it helps prepare students for future struggles.

All other options are incorrect because they don’t suit the context.

questions.question: Institutions are quite ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3, i.e., **‘alarming’.**

The sentence given is **‘The reports of incidents of rage in some of the reputed professional colleges and educational institutions are quite ______’.**

Since these institutions are said to be reputed, instances of ragging can only cause shock and worry. ‘Alarming’ is the most suitable word in this context.

All other options are incorrect because they don’t suit the context.

questions.question: It is a matter of ______ that
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4, i.e., **‘shame’.**

The sentence given is **‘It is a matter of ______ that even though ragging has been criticized for decades, we still come across such incidents’.**

The sentence talks about how ragging has been criticized for decades. Keeping that in mind, any more incidents of ragging can only be a matter of shame.

Thus, the correct answer is ‘shame’.

All other options- ‘pride’, ‘honour’, and ‘growth’- are incorrect because they don’t suit the context.

questions.question: Across such incidents of ______ torture.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1, i.e., **‘inhuman’.**

The sentence given is **‘It is a matter of shame that even though ragging has been criticized for decades, we still come across such incidents of ______ torture’.**

As the sentence talks about torture, the adjective to be used to describe it must be negative.

In this context, ‘inhuman’ is the correct answer.

Options 2 and 3- ‘humane’ and ‘relational’- don’t suit the context. Option 4 is incorrect because the word ‘objectional’ doesn’t exist.

questions.question: Ragging has become a ______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2, i.e., **‘dreadful’.**

The sentence given is **‘ragging has become a ______ affair in the institutions of higher learning’.**

Considering that the entire passage is about the harms of ragging, ‘dreadful’ suits the context and is the right answer.

Options 1, 3, and 4 (‘pleasant’, ‘wonderful’, and ‘comforting’) are incorrect because they don’t suit the context.

questions.question: Drug addiction is a social______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1, i.e., **‘evil’.**

The passage talks about the harms of drug addiction and in this context, ‘social evil’ which means ‘a problem or a malaise that affects the society’ is the best suited.

Option 2, or ‘myth’ is incorrect because the sentence then dismisses drug addiction as a trivial problem while the passage only stresses on the gravity of the problem.

Option 3, or ‘disease’ is incorrect because in order to describe social problems, the word ‘social’ is used with ‘evil’ but never with ‘disease’.

Option 4, or ‘idea’ is incorrect because it doesn’t suit the context.

questions.question: It has been prevalent in society from time ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2, i.e., **‘immemorial’.**

‘From time immemorial’ means ‘since forever’, and it suits the context of describing drug addiction as a problem which has existed for a very long time.

All other options are incorrect because they give rise to invalid or meaningless expressions.

questions.question: A drug addict becomes a drug ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 3, i.e., **‘dependent’.**

The sentences given to us are **‘A drug addict becomes a drug ______. He cannot live without drugs’.**

The very next sentence talks about how a drug addict cannot live without drugs. Thus, the right word is ‘dependent’.

All other words- ‘associate’, ‘relative’, and ‘independent’- are incorrect because they don’t suit the context.

questions.question: He cannot live without drugs. It is a form of ______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4, i.e., **‘psychological’.**

The sentences given to us are **‘He cannot live without drugs. It is a form of ______ conditioning that implies a set of mental and behavioural responses to drugs and related stimuli that result from repeated reinforcement produced by the use of drugs’.**

Words like ‘conditioning’, ‘mental and behavioural responses’,’stimuli’, and ‘reinforcement’ tell us that the context is psychological. Thus, ‘psychological’ is the correct answer.

All other options- ‘political’, ‘physical’, and ‘economical’- are incorrect.

questions.question: Chronic intoxication ______ to the individual
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1, i.e., ‘detrimental’.

The sentence given is **‘The World Health Organisation has defined drug abuse as a state of periodic, chronic intoxication, ______ to the individual and to the society, produced by ______ consumption of drugs either natural or synthetic’.**

The passage discusses the harms of drug abuse. In such a context, ‘detrimental’ (which means ‘harmful’) is the right word. Drugs are ‘detrimental to the individual and to the society’.

All other options- ‘crucial’, ‘beneficial’, and ‘influential’- are incorrect as they don’t fit in with the context.

questions.question: Produced by ______ consumption of drugs
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2, i.e., **‘repeated’.**

The sentence given is **‘The World Health Organisation has defined drug abuse as a state of periodic, chronic intoxication, detrimental to the individual and to the society, produced by ______ consumption of drugs either natural or synthetic’.**

The passage talks about how a drug addict cannot live without drugs and in the given context, ‘repeated consumption’ is the most suitable fit. Thus, ‘repeated’ is the correct answer.

All other options- ‘mere’, ‘rare’, and ‘occasionally’- are incorrect as they don’t suit the context.

questions.question: There are a number of causes which ______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3, i.e., **‘lead’.**

The sentence given is **‘There are a number of causes which ______ to drug addiction’.**

The context and the preposition ‘to’ tell us that the right word is ‘lead’.

All other options either don’t make sense (‘sort/perform to drug addiction’) or make the sentence grammatically incorrect (‘ensure to drug addiction’).

questions.question: There is a strong ______ between drug
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4, i.e., **‘nexus’.**

The sentence given is **‘There is a strong ______ between drug and torn family life’. **

The passage talks about the harms of the drug addiction, and the sentence mentions ‘torn family life’. In such a context, the word ‘nexus’, which means ‘a strong interrelationship’, is the most suited as it suggests a close relationship between drugs and a torn family life.

All other options- ‘interruption’, ‘dissonance’, and ‘conflict’- do not suit the context.

questions.question: One to ______ to drug.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1, i.e., **‘resort’.**

The sentence given is **‘It has been found that broken family structure often forces one to ______ to drug’.**

In the given context, the right word is ‘resort’. To ‘resort to’ something is to ‘take recourse to it’.

A broken family structure can force one to ‘resort’ or ‘take’ to drugs.

All other options- ‘place’, ‘deter’, or ‘reign’- either make the sentence grammatically incorrect or don’t suit the context.

questions.question: Euphoric or mind-altering ______ to
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2, i.e., **‘effect’.**

The sentence given to us is **‘This is because a person faced with such situation chooses drug for its euphoric or mind-altering ______ to escape from the immediate situation’.**

The sentence talks about the reasons for which a person chooses drugs. In such a context, mind-altering ‘effect’ is the most suitable answer.

People choose drugs for the effect of euphoria they produce.

All other options- ‘cause’, ‘affect’, or ‘result’- don’t suit the context.
